simple.meaning: עֻלְפֶּה (ʻulpeh) is a Hebrew word meaning “an envelope , i.e. (figuratively) mourning.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֻלְפֶּה (H5969) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֻלְפֶּה (H5969) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֻלְפֶּה (ʻulpeh) / H5969 is traced through Ezekiel 31:15 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “The Lord Yahweh says: ‘In the day when he went down to Sheol * Sheol is the place of the dead. I caused a mourning. I covered the deep for him, and I restrained its rivers. The great waters were stopped. I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.
